summary: A New York Times investigation reported that OpenAI, Google and Meta cut corners to gather training data, including transcribing over a million hours of YouTube videos and discussing use of copyrighted works despite legal and policy concerns.
technical_summary: To obtain scarce text data, companies built a speech recognition tool (Whisper) to transcribe YouTube audio, broadened terms of service, and debated using copyrighted material without licenses. Staff raised concerns about platform rules and copyright.

notes: Based on anonymous sources; legality is contested and unresolved.

summary: A multi-year study alleges that gig platforms such as Uber and Amazon use data-driven algorithms to set personalized, variable pay, paying workers different amounts for the same work.
technical_summary: Platforms use granular worker data (when and how long they work, past pay accepted) to calculate wage offers predicted to induce desired behavior, producing opaque, personalized and unpredictable pay, which the author calls algorithmic wage discrimination.

technology.quote: calculate the exact wage rates necessary to incentivize desired behaviors

failure_mode.quote: Across firms, the opaque practices that constitute algorithmic wage discrimination raise central questions

harm_type.quote: workers are being paid different amounts for the same amount of work that is conducted for the same amount of time

affected_population.quote: workers are being paid different amounts for the same amount of work that is conducted for the same amount of time
For a growing number of low-income and subordinated racial minority work forces in the United States

notes: Allegations from academic research; Uber disputes the paper's premise.
